name: Hierarchical Text-to-Video Alignment Benchmark
description: In the area of video generation, text-to-video (T2V) alignment refers to the critical ability of producing content that is consistent with textual descriptions. Despite the development of various T2V methods, there is still a lacks of a systematic evaluation benchmark to comprehensively assess their alignment ability. In this study, we propose a hierarchical and multi-dimensional evaluation benchmark, with the aim to complement the shortcomings of existing evaluation protocols and consequently improve the video generation quality with respect to T2V alignment. The benchmark categorizes T2V alignment ability into four tiers-fundamental, action, relational, and temporal-covering a total of 13 evaluation dimensions. Coupled with 542 rigorously selected evaluation prompts and the automated binary scoring of Gemini 1.5 Pro, the proposed benchmark offers a comprehensive and objective assessment of T2V alignment. reputation: A recent benchmark proposal that is promising for structured T2V evaluation, but it is not yet a widely established community standard.
notes: Uses Gemini 1.5 Pro as an automated judge, so results depend on judge reliability and prompt design; benchmark is relatively new and may have limited cross-paper comparability.
